newsitem.title: CHINA: China city pushes to open subway before HK return.
newsitem.headline: China city pushes to open subway before HK return.

text.p: China's southern Guangzhou city has called for the first section of a new subway to be opened on June 28, just days before the nearby British colony of Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule, the China News Service said on Monday.
The recent roofing of the Number One line's Tiyu West station showed construction of the east-west artery was basically complete, the agency quoted Guangzhou Vice Mayor Chen Kaizhi as saying.
Chen had called on all units working on the subway to guarantee the opening on June 28 of the first section of subway line in the Guangdong provincial capital, it said.
Guangdong borders on the British territory of Hong Kong, which returns to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of colonial rule.

City officials said in 1995 that the Guangzhou Number One line was scheduled to open on the same day as Hong Kong's return, but in January said the 5.3-km (3.3-mile) section between Xilang and Huangsha would open in late June.
